questions.question: An athlete crosses a distance of 3600 m in 12 minutes. What is his speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 3600 m

Time = 12 minutes

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ We know that 1 km = 1000 m

⇒ 3600 m = (3600)/(1000)=3.6km

⇒ 1 hour = 60 minutes

⇒ So, 12 minutes = (12)/(60)=0.2 hrs

⇒ Speed of an athlete = (3.6)/(0.2)=18 km/h

**Hence, the speed of an athlete is 18 km/h.**

questions.question: A truck runs 492 km on 36 Litter of diesel. How many kilometres can it run on 33 Litter of diesel?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A truck runs 492 km on 36 Litter of diesel.

**Calculation:**

On 36 Litre of diesel it runs = 492 km.

On 1 Litre of diesel it runs = 492/36 km = 41/3 km

On 33 Litre of diesel it runs = (41/3) × 33 = 451 km

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Ram is travelling at a speed of 72 km per hour while Shyam is travelling at a speed of 90 km per hour. What is the difference in their speeds (in metres per second)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Ram = 72 km/h

Speed of Shyam = 90 km/h

**Concept Used:**

1 km/h = (1000)/(3600) m/sec

**Calculation:**

**⇒ **Difference in speed of Ram and Shyam = 90 – 72 = 18 km/h

⇒ Change km/h into m/sec by multiplying (1000)/(3600)

⇒ 18 km/h = 18 × (1000)/(3600) = 5 m/sec

**∴ The difference in their speeds (in metres per second) is 5 m/sec.**

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing an Object with Length

When a train crosses a platform, bridge, or tunnel, the total distance covered is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the object being crossed.

Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary man, pole, or tree, the total distance covered is equal to the length of the train alone.

Relative Speed

If two trains move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. If they move in the same direction, it is S₁ − S₂.

questions.question: The speeds of A and B are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5. A takes 30 minutes more than B to reach the destination. In how much time does A reach the destination?

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 200 m and 250 m are running on parallel rail tracks at speeds of 68 km/h and 50 km/h, respectively. In how much time (in seconds) will they cross each other if they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of first train = 200 m

Length of second train = 250 m

Speed of first train = 68 km/h

Speed of second train = 50 km/h

**Concept used:**

To convert speeds from km/h to m/s, we use the formula: speed in m/s = speed in km/h × 5/18

When both trains are running in the same direction, their relative speed = speed of first train - speed of second train.

**Formula used:**

Time taken to cross each other = Total distance / Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 68 - 50 = 18 km/hr

⇒ Speed in m/s = 18 × 5/18 = 5 m/s

Total distance to be covered for the trains to cross each other completely = sum of their lengths = 200 m + 250 m = 450 m

Time taken to cross each other = Total distance / Relative speed

⇒ Time = 450 / 5 = 90 seconds

**Hence, it will take 90 seconds for the two trains to cross each other.**

times = distance/speed

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 kmph and including stoppages, it is 54 kmph. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?

Stoppage time per hour = (Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed

Stoppage time = (60 − 54) ÷ 60

Stoppage time = 6 ÷ 60 hour

Stoppage time in minutes = (1/10) × 60 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 mins.**

 Without Stoppage (Speed: 60 kmph)
 
 Distance: 60 km in 60 mins
 
 With Stoppage (Speed: 54 kmph)
 
 Distance: 54 km

 
 Stop

 

 6 km gap
 Takes 6 mins

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ In 1 hour (60 mins), without stoppages, the bus covers a distance of 60 km.

⇒ In 1 hour (60 mins), with stoppages, the bus covers a distance of 54 km.

⇒ Loss in distance due to stoppages = 60 − 54 = 6 km.

⇒ Time required to cover this 6 km gap at the original speed is the actual stoppage time.

⇒ Stoppage time = Distance ÷ Original Speed

⇒ Stoppage time = 6 ÷ 60 hours = 1/10 hours.

⇒ Stoppage time in minutes = (1/10) × 60 = 6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 mins.**

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂). For equal time intervals, Average Speed = (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

For two bodies moving in the same direction, relative speed is |S₁ − S₂|. For bodies moving in opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.question: A person reaches his destination 30 minutes late, if his speed is 3 km/h, and reaches 30 minutes before time if his speed is 4 km/h. Find the distance of his destination from his starting point.

questions.question: A boat can travel 60km downstream in 4 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water is 13 km/h, then in what time will it cover 30 km upstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance downstream = 60 km

Time taken downstream = 4 hours

Speed of the boat in still water = 13 km/h

Distance to cover upstream = 30 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed downstream = Distance downstream / Time downstream

Speed downstream = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

Speed upstream = Speed of boat in still water - Speed of stream

Time upstream = Distance upstream / Speed upstream

**Calculation:**

Speed downstream = 60 km / 4 h

Speed downstream = 15 km/h

Speed downstream = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

15 km/h = 13 km/h + Speed of stream

Speed of stream = 15 km/h - 13 km/h

Speed of stream = 2 km/h

Speed upstream = Speed of boat in still water - Speed of stream

Speed upstream = 13 km/h - 2 km/h

Speed upstream = 11 km/h

Time upstream = Distance upstream / Speed upstream

Time upstream = 30 km / 11 km/h

Time upstream = (30)/(11) hours

Time upstream = 2 (8)/(11) hours

**The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: Ravi can row a boat in still water at the speed of 14 km/h. If a river is flowing at the sped of 2 km/h and Ravi takes 3 hours to cover a certain distance upstream, then how much time will he take to cover the same distance downstream?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of the boat = 14kmph 

Flow of the river = 2 kmph

Ravi takes 3 hours to cover a certain distance upstream

Concept used:

Distance = Time × Speed

While going upstream, the speed of a boat and the flow of the river get added to calculate the effective speed. On the other hand, while going downstream, to take the effective speed, the difference between the speed of the boat and the flow of the river is considered. 

Calculation:

Effective speed during the upstream journey = (14 - 2) kmph = 12kmph

Distance covered = 12 × 3 = 36 hours

Effective speed during the downstream journey = (14 + 2) kmph = 16kmph

So, time taken by Ravi to cover 36 km downstream = 36 ÷ 16 = 2.25 hours = 2 hours 15 minutes

**∴ Ravi will take 2 hours 15 minutes to cover the same distance downstream.**
